questions.text: Question 1: select the one statement that best describes you.

scale.label: I don't feel self-conscious about my weight or body size when I'm with others.
I feel concerned about how I look to others, but it normally does not make me feel disappointed with myself.
I do get self-conscious about my appearance and weight, which makes me feel disappointed in myself.
I feel very self-conscious about my weight and frequently feel intense shame and disgust for myself; I try to avoid social contacts because of my self-consciousness.

questions.text: Question 2: select the one statement that best describes you.

scale.label: I don't have difficulty eating slowly in the proper manner.
Although I seem to gobble down foods, I don't end up feeling stuffed because of eating too much.
At times, I tend to eat quickly and then feel uncomfortably full afterwards.
I bolt down my food without really chewing it and usually feel uncomfortably stuffed.

questions.text: Question 3: select the one statement that best describes you.

scale.label: I feel capable of controlling my eating urges when I want to.
I feel I have failed to control my eating more than the average person.
I feel utterly helpless about controlling my eating urges.
Because I feel helpless about controlling my eating, I have become very desperate about trying to get in control.

questions.text: Question 4: select the one statement that best describes you.

scale.label: I don't have a habit of eating when I'm bored.
I sometimes eat when bored, but can often get busy and take my mind off food.
I regularly eat when bored, but occasionally can use another activity to take my mind off eating.
I have a strong habit of eating when bored; nothing seems to help me break it.

questions.text: Question 5: select the one statement that best describes you.

scale.label: I'm usually physically hungry when I eat something.
Occasionally, I eat on impulse even though I am not hungry.
I regularly eat foods I may not enjoy to satisfy a hungry feeling even though physically I don't need food.
Even when not physically hungry, I get a hunger feeling in my mouth that seems satisfied only by eating; sometimes I spit out the food to avoid gaining weight.

questions.text: Question 6: select the one statement that best describes you.

scale.label: I don't feel guilt or self-hate after I overeat.
After I overeat, I occasionally feel guilt or self-hate.
Almost all the time I experience strong guilt or self-hate after I overeat.

questions.text: Question 7: select the one statement that best describes you.

scale.label: I don't lose total control of my eating when dieting, even after periods when I overeat.
Sometimes when I eat a forbidden food on a diet, I feel I have blown it and eat even more.
I frequently tell myself I have blown it and eat even more.
I regularly start strict diets but break them by binge eating; my life seems to be feast or famine.

questions.text: Question 8: select the one statement that best describes you.

scale.label: I rarely eat so much that I feel uncomfortably stuffed afterwards.
Usually about once a month, I eat such a quantity that I feel very stuffed.
I regularly have periods when I eat large amounts at meals or snacks.
I eat so much that I regularly feel quite uncomfortable and sometimes nauseous.

questions.text: Question 9: select the one statement that best describes you.

scale.label: My calorie intake does not regularly go very high or very low.
Sometimes after overeating, I try to reduce my calorie intake almost to nothing.
I regularly overeat at night and am not hungry in the morning.
In adulthood, I have had week-long periods of near-starvation following periods of overeating; it seems like feast or famine.

questions.text: Question 10: select the one statement that best describes you.

scale.label: I can usually stop eating when I want to; I know when enough is enough.
Every so often, I feel a compulsion to eat that I can't seem to control.
I frequently experience strong urges to eat that I seem unable to control, though at other times I can control them.
I feel incapable of controlling urges to eat and fear not being able to stop voluntarily.

questions.text: Question 11: select the one statement that best describes you.

scale.label: I have no problem stopping when I feel full.
I usually stop when full but occasionally overeat and feel uncomfortably stuffed.
I have a problem stopping once I start and usually feel uncomfortably stuffed after a meal.
Because I have trouble stopping, I sometimes induce vomiting to relieve a stuffed feeling.

questions.text: Question 12: select the one statement that best describes you.

scale.label: I eat just as much with others as when by myself.
Sometimes I eat less with others because I am self-conscious.
I frequently eat only a small amount around others because I am embarrassed.
I feel so ashamed about overeating that I choose times when no one will see me; I feel like a closet eater.

questions.text: Question 13: select the one statement that best describes you.

scale.label: I eat three meals a day with only an occasional snack.
I eat three meals a day and normally snack between meals.
When snacking heavily, I get in the habit of skipping regular meals.
There are regular periods when I seem to eat continually, with no planned meals.

questions.text: Question 14: select the one statement that best describes you.

scale.label: I don't think much about controlling unwanted eating urges.
Sometimes I feel preoccupied with trying to control my eating urges.
I frequently spend much time thinking about how much I ate or trying not to eat more.
Most waking hours are preoccupied with thoughts about eating or not eating; I constantly struggle not to eat.

questions.text: Question 15: select the one statement that best describes you.

scale.label: I don't think about food a great deal.
I have strong food cravings, but they last only briefly.
I have days when I can't seem to think about anything else but food.
Most days seem preoccupied with thoughts about food; I feel like I live to eat.

questions.text: Question 16: select the one statement that best describes you.

scale.label: I usually know whether or not I'm physically hungry. I take the right portion of food to satisfy me.
Occasionally, I feel uncertain about knowing whether or not I'm physically hungry. At these times it is hard to know how much food I should take to satisfy me.
Even though I might know how many calories I should eat, I do not have any idea what is a normal amount of food for me.
